problem: The figure caption promises hard acids and bases on one side and soft acids and bases on the other, but the 'Hard' set contains only cations (H+, Mg2+, Al3+) and the 'Soft' set mixes cations (Ag+, Hg2+) with an anion (I−). A student can read the soft set as 'soft acids' and be confused about whether I− is an acid.
fix: Keep acids and bases consistent on both sides, e.g. Hard: H+, Mg2+, Al3+, F−, OH−; Soft: Ag+, Hg2+, I−, S2−; overlap: Fe2+, Cu2+. Or label the sets 'Hard acids and bases' and 'Soft acids and bases' and put only acids in each, with hard/soft bases listed separately in the text.

problem: Pb2+ is called a soft metal, but in the standard Pearson classification Pb2+ is borderline, not soft. Chelation therapy for lead in fact uses hard O donors (EDTA) as well as soft S donors, which contradicts the sentence as written.
fix: Write: 'toxic metals such as Hg2+ (soft) and Pb2+ (borderline, so it binds both O and S donors)'.
